content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working on a solution for controlling a two-stage HVAC system. I have a packaged AC unit with two separate refrigeration circuits (two compressors and two reversing valves) and am seeking more manual control than what the installed [company_name] controller currently allows. I've started an automation program, attached here, and this is my first experience with automation—so my configuration may need improvement! My objectives are: manual and automatic control for heat, auto, and cool modes; momentary on/off inputs; using a room sensor to determine heating/cooling stages ([company_name] temperature sensor); a return air sensor; a timer that ensures the system does not stay on indefinitely; a standby timer to allow system equalization before restarting; and integration of a fresh air damper with variable 0-10V input. My current program works except for the fresh air damper integration—I would appreciate suggestions on how to handle this part. Also, my compressor timing logic may be overly simple. Any feedback or advice would be welcomed—I'm still learning.

Hello, I can't provide details specifically about the [company_name] controller you mentioned, but I have successfully managed two ventilation systems using the [company_name] logic controller and module. The logic module handled system blocking and synchronized operation between the controller and peripherals. Please note: the module is compatible with pt100 and pt1000 sensors; however, I'm not certain if it will work with Ni1000 temperature sensors. If possible, please share the schematic of your current setup. I think it's feasible to accomplish your objectives with this kind of module.

Hello, I've reviewed the product range you mentioned. The largest controller in the range still only offers five inputs. My current setup matches the diagram attached from the controller manual. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants discuss achieving flexible manual and automatic control of a two-stage HVAC system using [company_name] automation hardware, seeking improvements over the basic functions of their current controller. They focus on integration of sensors, implementing sophisticated timed operations, and enhancing damper control with variable input signal. Users express uncertainty regarding damper integration and compressor timing methods, highlighting a need for clearer documentation and greater product flexibility to support new users.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants the automation system hardware and software to support both manual/automatic operation for heating and cooling, quick and responsive mode selection, integration with temperature and return air sensors, safety timers to prevent unintended running and ensure proper system delays, and smooth connectivity to a fresh air damper with a variable-input actuator.
